q1.q: Is IELTiva an official IELTS product?
q1.a: No. IELTiva is an independent preparation platform. It isn't affiliated with or endorsed by the IELTS partners.

q2.a: You can create an account, follow published courses, plan your study and track your progress. Timed practice, writing feedback and mock tests are still being built.

q3.q: Will IELTiva predict my band score?
q3.a: Not yet. Band estimates will only appear once they've been validated against human-marked samples. Until then, feedback focuses on what you can improve.

q4.q: Does it cover Academic and General Training?
q4.a: Yes. Choose your test type in your settings, and courses can be filtered to match it.

q5.a: Creating an account is free. Prices for prepaid packages will be published before they go on sale, and there's no subscription.

final.title: Your next step is one small task

reading.title: Reading preview

questions.prompt: Roofs in cities were once used mainly for gardens.
Plants on a roof can reduce the need for cooling.
Soil on green roofs holds rainwater for several days.
What can make a repair to a green roof difficult?
options: The garden may have to be lifted

questions.prompt: Critics say that savings depend on the local:

reading.instructions: Answer the questions using information from the passage.
paragraphs: In many crowded cities, the flat roofs of offices and apartment blocks have long been empty spaces, used for little more than water tanks and air-conditioning units. Over the past two decades, however, planners have begun to see them differently. A growing number of these roofs now hold soil, plants and sometimes small vegetable plots.

The attraction is partly practical. Plants absorb a large share of the sunlight that would otherwise heat a building, so the rooms below need less cooling in summer. Soil also holds rainwater for several hours, which reduces the pressure on city drains during heavy storms.

Installing a green roof is not simple. The structure must be strong enough to carry wet soil, and waterproofing has to be replaced if it fails, which can mean lifting the whole garden. For these reasons, the cost is usually higher than for a conventional roof, at least at first.

Supporters argue that the expense is recovered over time, since a protected roof surface tends to last longer. Critics reply that the savings depend heavily on local climate. In cooler regions, they point out, a building may benefit far less.

calibration.defaultTargets: Each dataset covers one IELTS type and one task, so they're never pooled.
calibration.targets: Targets: {samples} samples, error of {mae} or less, {within} within one band.
calibration.targetsNotApproved: Not yet approved by an instructor.
calibration.approveTargetsBody: Confirm these targets as an instructor. They're internal targets, not official IELTS standards.
calibration.referenceHint: A neutral code. Never use a student's name.
calibration.deidentifyNote: Remove all identifying details first. Add only work whose writer gave consent.
calibration.freezeBody: A frozen dataset can never change. Every sample needs its final mark first.
calibration.markNote: You can't see other markers' marks. Two different qualified markers must mark each sample.
calibration.approveRunBody: Confirm as an instructor that you've reviewed this run.
calibration.releaseInternalBody: Only people allowed to manage releases will see these bands, labelled as unvalidated.
calibration.releasePublicBody: Students will see bands for this exact model, prompt, IELTS type and task. This needs every safeguard to be met.
calibration.listenNote: Mark what you hear. Pronunciation cannot be judged from the transcript.
calibration.pronunciationResult: {count} samples compared and {skipped} skipped. Correlation with human marks: {correlation}.
calibration.pronunciationNote: This compares the speech service's measure with what qualified markers heard. It is evidence for instructors to weigh. It does not validate anything by itself, and cannot release a band.

analytics.title: My progress

guide.ESTIMATED: An approximate band for practice only. It is not an official IELTS result and can differ from your real score.
guide.REVIEWED: A score checked by a qualified instructor. It is still not an official IELTS result.
